vision: An OTP-native task-execution engine an AI orchestrator drives end to end: it pulls tasks from the rmap roadmap, dispatches each to a headless coding agent running in an isolated worktree, runs the target project's own check stack against the result, and reports verified outcomes back over an agent-shaped surface (MCP tools / JSON CLI). harness is itself developed by dogfooding — from the core loop (Task 8) onward, every pending roadmap task is delivered by dispatching it through harness rather than hand-building it.

contract-proof.description: Conformance suite + a second adapter (Codex) — prove the AgentAdapter contract holds for two implementors before resilience builds on it

core-loop.description: Worktree lifecycle, rmap ingestion, verification runner, supervised run lifecycle

deferred.description: Parked work — revisit after the core milestones ship

multi-agent.description: Cursor and Grok adapters, capability + availability registry with quota fail-over

resilience.description: Batch fan-out, failure-classified retry, autonomous repair loop

scaffold.description: mix project scaffold + standard dep stack

surface.description: Agent-shaped MCP/CLI surface, human status view, run logging

task.title: Scaffold the OTP application + standard dep stack
acceptance_criteria: `mix compile` is clean
`mix test` runs the default suite green
Styler is first in the `.formatter.exs` plugins list
The supervision tree starts under `Application`
task.body: Scaffold `harness` as an Elixir OTP application with a supervision tree — it orchestrates long-lived agent runs, so it needs one. Add the standard project dep stack and tooling per the global Elixir setup conventions (Styler, Credo, Dialyxir, Doctor, ex_unit_json, dialyzer_json, descripex, Sobelow, and Reach as a dev/test analysis dep), wired into `mix.exs`, `.formatter.exs`, and `cli/0` preferred_envs. Generate the baseline `.gitignore`, `README.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.
task.implemented: Scaffolded OTP application with supervision tree, full standard dep stack (styler first, credo, dialyxir, doctor, sobelow, reach + boxart, ex_dna/ex_ast, descripex, tidewave+bandit), cli/0, dialyzer :apps_direct + priv/plts, all quality gates green (compile, test, format, credo --strict, doctor, sobelow, dialyzer 0 warnings).

task.title: Evaluate orchestration libraries — confirm thin-core
acceptance_criteria: Each candidate skimmed for whether it offers anything the thin OTP core doesn't
A written build-vs-adopt decision with rationale
Any borrowed design ideas are recorded with their source
A determination on whether `claude_code` / `codex_sdk` are CLI wrappers or native reimplementations, with a uniform-Ports-vs-SDK recommendation
out_of_scope: Writing any adapter or orchestration code — this task is evaluation only
Adding any candidate library as a dependency
task.body: Skim the source and docs of the candidate Elixir orchestration libraries — `opal`, `gen_agent` + `gen_agent_ensemble`, `altar_ai`, `ex_mcp`. The harness core is deliberately thin — a Port per run, a `gen_statem` per run, a `DynamicSupervisor` for batches, all stock OTP — and harness no longer needs a normalized event model, so the expected outcome is build-thin-core rather than adopt. Confirm that, and record any design ideas worth borrowing. Also settle the per-agent SDK question: determine whether `claude_code` and `codex_sdk` are CLI wrappers around the headless binary or native reimplementations. If they are wrappers, harness gains nothing from them — its raw-passthrough design discards an SDK's normalized event model, and OTP Ports already spawn the binary with better termination signals — so every adapter uses uniform Ports; only a native reimplementation that removes the external-binary dependency would justify the dep. Record both decisions in a concept doc.
task.implemented: Evaluated opal, gen_agent, gen_agent_ensemble, altar_ai, ex_mcp + the claude_code/codex_sdk SDKs. Outcome: build thin core, adopt none, uniform Ports for all adapters. claude_code and codex_sdk confirmed CLI wrappers (not native reimpls). Decision + borrowed design ideas recorded in docs/orchestration-library-evaluation.md.

task.title: Define the AgentAdapter behaviour — invocation + capture
acceptance_criteria: An `AgentAdapter` behaviour with documented callbacks for invoke / capture / terminate
Raw agent output is passed through untouched — no per-agent event normalization
A capability declaration each adapter fills in
Nothing Claude-specific leaks into the contract
out_of_scope: Any normalized or typed event model — explicitly cut
task.body: Define the core contract every agent adapter implements — a `behaviour` that, given a task spec plus run options, builds the agent's headless command line, spawns it, detects termination, and hands back the raw captured output plus wall-clock duration. Deliberately no normalized event model: harness does not parse or remap each agent's JSON — the consumer is an AI that reads raw transcripts natively, and harness derives run success from its own verification stack, not the agent's self-reported result. The behaviour also declares per-adapter capabilities (session resume, permission modes, and so on). Contract only — no concrete adapter.
task.implemented: Defined the Harness.AgentAdapter behaviour: 4 callbacks (capabilities/0, build_command/1, classify_message/2, terminate/1) plus generic AgentAdapter.invoke/2 (Port spawn) and supports?/2. Structs: Invocation, Run, Capabilities. Raw passthrough, no event model; :error vs :terminated split for retry classification; session-token extraction and version/0 probe deferred. No concrete adapter. The use-macro from the plan was dropped — Doctor's 100% spec gate does not pair @spec to a defmacro; adapters declare @behaviour directly.

task.title: Build the Claude Code headless adapter
acceptance_criteria: A headless prompt run captures raw output and reports termination
Working directory and permission mode are wired
Session resume works across two runs
Termination is derived from process exit + timeout, not `$?`
An idle timeout kills a run that emits no output for a configurable window, separate from the total-run budget
task.body: Implement the first concrete adapter — driving Claude Code headlessly via `claude -p` over Ports. Capture the raw output stream and hand it back unparsed. Wire working directory, permission mode, and session resume/continue. Detect termination from the process/Port closing plus two timeout guards — a total-run budget, and an idle timeout that kills a run emitting no output for a configurable window — never from the exit code, which is known to be unreliable.
task.implemented: Built Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude (claude -p, stream-json, --permission-mode bypassPermissions, --continue resume), the generic Harness.AgentAdapter.Driver enforcing total + idle timeout guards, the Outcome result struct, and the shared OSProcess port-lifecycle helper. Resume resolves the behaviour's session-token deferral via --continue (no new callback). 100% test + doc coverage; integration test green against real claude.

task.title: Worktree-per-job lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: Each run gets its own isolated git worktree
Concurrent runs do not collide on the working tree
Worktrees are cleaned up on success and retained on failure (configurable)
A crashed run does not leak an orphan worktree
task.body: harness runs every job in an isolated git worktree so concurrent agent runs never collide and the verification stack has a clean checkout to grade. Implement worktree creation per run, dispatch of the agent into it, and a keep-or-tear-down decision on completion (retain on failure for inspection; configurable). This is the automation of the repo's existing worktree-per-branch convention.
task.implemented: Harness.Worktree (create/2, finish/3, remove/1, retained?/1, base_dir/1) for per-run isolated git worktrees + Harness.Worktree.Sweeper boot-time orphan reaper. Harness.Git subprocess wrapper. Configurable via :harness, :worktree app env + HARNESS_WORKTREE_ROOT. 48 tests, coverage 100/93.6/85.2%.

task.title: rmap task ingestion
acceptance_criteria: harness fetches a task — by id, or the next pending one — from the rmap roadmap
The task renders to an agent-ready prompt suitable for the adapter
Ingestion reads the rmap source — it does not duplicate the roadmap
task.body: Let harness pull a task straight from the rmap roadmap — read `roadmap/tasks.toml` / `roadmap/data.json` (or shell out to `rmap`) and render the task as a ready-to-run agent prompt. `rmap delegate <id> --to <agent>` already emits a paste-ready prompt; harness consumes that instead of a human copy-pasting it. This is the input half of the loop — the roadmap becomes the job queue.
task.implemented: Added Harness.Roadmap.ingest/2 + Harness.Roadmap.Item. Shells out to rmap (show/next/delegate) with explicit --tasks-path; fetches a task by id or next-pending and renders the rmap delegate prompt verbatim. Error taxonomy: invalid_agent/invalid_selector/rmap_not_found/no_pending_task/task_not_found/roadmap_not_found/rmap_failed/rmap_bad_output. Covered by a unit suite with fixture roadmaps under test/fixtures/.

task.title: Verification runner — run the target project's check stack
acceptance_criteria: A configurable list of check commands runs against a given worktree
An Elixir preset is provided as the default check set
Each check's pass/fail and output are captured into a structured verdict
Any red check makes the overall verdict red
out_of_scope: Feeding failures back to the agent — that is the autonomous repair loop task
task.body: After an agent finishes, harness runs the target project's own check stack against its worktree and produces a structured pass/fail — this is what makes "did the job succeed?" objective and agent-agnostic, instead of trusting the agent's self-report. The check set is a configurable list of commands; ship an Elixir preset (`mix test.json`, `mix dialyzer.json`, doctor, sobelow, credo). Aggregate each check's result into one verdict the run lifecycle can gate on.
task.implemented: Harness.Verification grades a worktree by running a configurable check stack and aggregating per-check Results into a Verdict (any red => red). Ships elixir_preset/0: mix test.json, dialyzer.json, credo --strict, doctor, sobelow --exit. Each check is spawned over an OTP port bounded by an absolute per-check deadline (default 600_000 ms) so a hung check — idle or still streaming output — is killed rather than wedging the run; System.cmd was rejected as uninterruptible and subprocess-orphaning. Each Result carries a kind (:exited | :timed_out | :not_launched) so a consumer can distinguish a retryable timeout from a genuine red check. Check/Result/Verdict structs + config under :harness, :verification. 19 tests, 94% coverage.

task.title: Supervised run lifecycle process
acceptance_criteria: One job = one supervised `gen_statem` with observable state
It drives worktree → adapter → verification and settles on a verdict
A crashing run is isolated from siblings
Per-run timeout and external cancellation both work
task.body: Implement the supervised process that owns one job end to end — model it as a `gen_statem` moving through `dispatched → running → verifying → {done | failed}`. It creates the worktree, spawns the adapter, waits for termination, runs the verification stack, and settles on a verdict. Crash isolation (a failed run never touches siblings), a per-run timeout, and external cancellation. The run state must be observable. Completing this task is the single-agent core loop working end to end for one task; the contract-proof bundle (conformance suite + Codex adapter) then proves the adapter contract holds on a second agent.
task.implemented: Harness.Run :gen_statem owns one job end to end (dispatched → running → verifying → done/failed): carves the isolated worktree, dispatches the agent via AgentAdapter.Driver, runs the verification stack, settles a verdict. Harness.Run.Supervisor (one_for_one DynamicSupervisor, :temporary children) gives crash isolation between concurrent runs; a Registry maps run-id → pid; a Task.Supervisor parents every per-step async task so a crashing step is an event, not a crash. cancel/1 and a per-run lifetime-budget timeout both abort cleanly and SIGKILL the agent; status/1 exposes live state. AgentAdapter.Driver gained an :on_spawn hook so the lifecycle process can capture the run handle for cancellation. Verification is the sole grader — a timed-out agent is still verified. 23 new tests; suite green; dialyzer/credo/doctor clean.

task.title: Batch orchestrator with concurrency cap
acceptance_criteria: A batch of N tasks runs under a concurrency cap of M
Partial failure is tolerated — the batch completes and reports per-task status
Per-task verdicts are collected into one batch result
task.body: Implement the batch layer — fan a set of tasks out across run-lifecycle processes under a `DynamicSupervisor`, with a configurable concurrency cap, and collect the per-task verdicts. Tolerate partial failure: one failed or red run must not abort the batch; the batch result reports every task's outcome. A batch is typically an rmap bundle or an `rmap next-bundle` result.
task.implemented: Harness.Batch.run/4 + Harness.Batch.Result — fans tasks out across supervised Harness.Run children under a concurrency cap, tolerates partial failure (red/crashed run never aborts the batch), collects one Run.Result per task in input order. Delivered via parallel multi-agent dogfood, driven by Codex; commit on harness/run-1779373868703-29f9a9b0.

task.title: Retry policy with failure classification
acceptance_criteria: Failures are classified as transient, quota-exhausted, or terminal
Transient failures retry with capped exponential backoff
Quota exhaustion stops retrying that agent at once — no backoff loop against a multi-hour wall
Terminal failures are not retried
The policy is configurable per batch or per run
task.body: Add a per-run retry policy that first classifies the failure. Transient failures (a process crash, a flaky check) retry with capped exponential backoff. Quota exhaustion — a subscription agent hitting its cap — is NOT retryable on a useful timescale (the reset window is hours); it must stop retrying that agent immediately, marked for fail-over rather than backoff. Genuine terminal task failures are never retried. Make the policy injectable per batch or per run.
task.implemented: Harness.Run.RetryPolicy + Harness.Run.FailureClass — classifies a failed run transient/quota_exhausted/terminal; transient retries with capped exponential backoff, quota stops at once for fail-over, terminal never retried; policy injectable per run/batch via :harness, :retry_policy. Delivered via parallel multi-agent dogfood, driven by Cursor; commit on harness/run-1779373868714-f42cdd07.

task.title: Autonomous repair loop
acceptance_criteria: A red verdict triggers a repair attempt — failures fed back via session resume
The loop stops on green or at the attempt cap
A quota or terminal failure ends the loop instead of burning attempts
The number of repair attempts is configurable
task.body: Close the verify loop. When verification comes back red, feed the failing checks' output back to the same agent via session resume and re-run, up to a configurable attempt cap. The objective check stack is the grader, so an agent iterating against it is not self-grading. Stop on green, on the attempt cap, or on a non-repairable failure class (e.g. quota exhaustion — hand to fail-over instead).
task.implemented: Harness.Run repair loop + Harness.Run.RepairPrompt — a red verdict resumes the same agent with the failing checks fed back, re-commits and re-grades up to :max_repair_attempts (default 2); stops on green, the cap, or a non-repairable failure. Delivered via parallel multi-agent dogfood, driven by Claude; commit on harness/run-1779373868724-a4ceeede.

task.title: Reusable adapter conformance test suite
acceptance_criteria: A shared conformance module parameterized by adapter
The Claude adapter passes the full suite
Invocation, capture, termination, timeout, and adapter-level cancellation (`terminate` kills an in-flight run) are all covered
task.body: Build a reusable test module every `AgentAdapter` implementation must pass — exercising invocation, raw-output capture, termination detection, timeout, and adapter-level cancellation (the behaviour's `terminate` callback killing an in-flight run and releasing its Port/process). This is adapter-scope only: external cancellation *orchestration* — a caller telling the running system to cancel a job — is the supervised lifecycle's concern (Task 8) and is out of scope here. Run the Claude adapter against the suite. This suite is the gate Codex and every later adapter (Cursor, Grok, ACP) are held to: a leak gets fixed in the behaviour, not patched around in the adapter.
task.implemented: Built Harness.AgentAdapter.ConformanceCase — a reusable, adapter-parameterized conformance suite (use ConformanceCase, adapter: M) covering invocation, verbatim raw-output capture, termination detection, timeout (terminate/1 as the driver's timeout-branch handler), and adapter-level cancellation. Contract checks are agent-free (synthesized port messages + /bin/sleep stand-in); one :integration test drives the real agent through Driver.run/3. Run against the Claude adapter (ClaudeConformanceTest) and Harness.FakeAdapter (FakeAdapterConformanceTest, proving reusability). Made FakeAdapter contract-faithful (build_command/1 now rejects undeclared permission modes). Trimmed ClaudeTest to Claude-specific assertions. Delivered by harness's first fully-green dogfood run (run-1779367169148-29cf0bea).

task.title: Cursor headless adapter
acceptance_criteria: A Cursor run captures raw output and reports termination
The adapter passes the conformance suite with no changes to the suite
Any abstraction leak is fixed in the behaviour, not patched around
task.body: Implement the Cursor adapter — drive `cursor-agent` in headless/print mode over Ports (no Elixir SDK exists), capture raw output, declare its capabilities. It extends the contract — already proven in Phase 2 against Claude and Codex — to a third agent, and must pass the conformance suite unchanged.
task.implemented: Harness.AgentAdapter.Cursor — drives cursor-agent -p over Ports; --force --trust for unattended runs, --continue resume. Delivered via parallel dogfood run run-1779369258533-24f56b83; 5/5 verification checks green, conformance suite passed unchanged.

task.title: Codex headless adapter
acceptance_criteria: A Codex run captures raw output and reports termination
The adapter passes the conformance suite unchanged
Any abstraction leak surfaced is fixed in the behaviour, not the adapter
task.body: Implement the Codex adapter — drive `codex exec` over Ports, capture raw output, declare capabilities. This is harness's second adapter and the first real test of the `AgentAdapter` contract: Codex's invocation (`codex exec --json`) is the most different from Claude's, so building it now — while only the Claude adapter depends on the behaviour — shakes out any Claude-specific leak before Phase 3's resilience layer couples to the contract. Must pass the conformance suite unchanged — a leak is fixed in the behaviour, not patched around in the adapter.
task.implemented: Harness.AgentAdapter.Codex — drives codex exec --json over Ports; resume swaps in 'exec resume --last'. Delivered via parallel dogfood run run-1779369258524-7c1a28d5; 5/5 verification checks green, conformance suite passed unchanged, no abstraction leak.

task.title: Grok headless adapter
acceptance_criteria: A Grok run captures raw output and reports termination
The adapter passes the conformance suite with no changes to the suite
Working directory, permission mode, and session resume are wired
task.body: Implement the Grok adapter — drive Grok Build headlessly (`grok -p`, or the `agent` subcommand) over Ports (no Elixir SDK exists), capture raw output. Wire working directory, permission mode, and session resume. Must pass the conformance suite unchanged. Grok-specific extras (`--best-of-n`, `--check`, worktree flags) are surfaced through the capability registry, not the core behaviour.
task.implemented: Harness.AgentAdapter.Grok — drives grok -p --output-format streaming-json over Ports; --permission-mode bypassPermissions, --continue resume. Delivered via parallel dogfood run run-1779369258542-cc4a6123; 5/5 verification checks green, conformance suite passed unchanged.

task.title: Capability + availability registry with quota fail-over
acceptance_criteria: Each adapter declares its capabilities
A run requesting an unsupported capability is rejected up front, not mid-run
A quota-exhausted agent is marked unavailable and the job fails over to a capable agent with headroom
Fail-over routing is observable
task.body: Add a registry the orchestrator queries before dispatch. Each adapter declares its capabilities (session resume, permission granularity, MCP/tool config, and so on) so a run requesting an unsupported capability is rejected up front with a clear error. The registry also tracks availability — when an agent hits its subscription quota, the orchestrator routes the job to another agent with headroom instead of failing it. This is the concrete payoff of running multiple adapters.

task.title: Agent-shaped surface — MCP tools + JSON CLI
acceptance_criteria: harness exposes typed MCP tools and a JSON-clean CLI from one `api()` definition
A caller can dispatch a single task or a batch and choose the target agent
Switching the target agent requires no code change
Progressive `describe()` disclosure (L1/L2/L3) works
task.body: Build harness's own entry point, shaped for an AI orchestrator as the primary consumer. Annotate harness's public functions with descripex `api()`, build a `Harness.Manifest`, and generate MCP tools via `Descripex.MCP.tools/1` served from harness's own MCP server (over Bandit), with progressive `describe()` disclosure. Provide a JSON-clean CLI from the same `api()` definitions. The target agent is a parameter, not a code change.

task.title: Human status view
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable view shows in-flight, green, red, and repairing runs
It surfaces why a run went red or an agent went unavailable
It does not require the human to parse raw JSON
task.body: A glanceable, human-readable view of harness state — what runs are in flight, what's green, what's red, what's repairing — so the human orchestrator has a window into the fleet without parsing JSON. The primary user is an agent, but the human still orchestrates; this is their dashboard. Keep it simple — a CLI status command or terminal view is enough.

task.title: Structured run logging + result persistence
acceptance_criteria: Each run emits a structured, queryable log record
Batch results are persisted and reloadable after the process exits
A run's failure cause is reconstructable from its record
The store is pluggable, file-backed by default
task.body: Add structured per-run logging (queryable records — agent, task, verdict, duration, repair attempts) and a result store so a finished batch's outcomes survive the process. Records must support the "understand why something happened" need — a red verdict, a fail-over, a quota block should all be reconstructable. Keep the store pluggable, file-backed by default; do not couple the core to a database.

task.title: Run telemetry + quota/cost accounting
out_of_scope: Per-token dollar cost accounting — agents run on flat subscriptions, there is nothing to bill
task.body: DEFERRED — out of scope until the core, batch, and multi-agent milestones ship. Subscription agents have no per-token marginal cost, so dollar accounting is meaningless. If this is ever picked up, it is quota-burn telemetry — how close each agent is to its cap, when the window resets — to make fail-over predictive rather than reactive. Revisit only if reactive fail-over (Task 16) proves insufficient.

task.title: ACP transport adapter
out_of_scope: Any work until ACP has meaningful cross-agent adoption
task.body: DEFERRED — speculative. Implement an adapter that speaks the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) via `ex_mcp` as an alternative transport to per-agent shell-outs. Its value depends on ACP adoption across agents; revisit once ACP is broadly supported. If picked up, it ships behind the same `AgentAdapter` behaviour and is held to the conformance suite like any other adapter.

task.title: Inject a harness-owned rule set into agent invocations
acceptance_criteria: The harness holds one canonical rule set; no rule content is hand-maintained per repo or per agent

Each adapter injects the rule set through its best available channel — a dedicated system-prompt flag where the CLI offers one (Claude's --append-system-prompt-file), else prompt-prepend or a generated ephemeral rule file in the worktree
The injected set is a curated, filterable subset — verification gates are excluded, since the verification runner enforces them
Two different agents dispatched by harness receive the same canonical rules without a hand-maintained rule file per repo
out_of_scope: Verification-gate enforcement — coverage, dialyzer, and credo thresholds are the verification runner's job (Task 7), checked not injected
Editing or deleting the user's own ~/.claude/includes/ files — what the harness injects is a harness-side decision, independent of the user's personal Claude Code config

Hand-maintained, committed per-repo rule files (a CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / Cursor rules file checked into every target repo) — that maintenance burden is what this task replaces; a harness-generated ephemeral rule file, rendered from the canonical source into a throwaway worktree and never committed, is in scope as a delivery channel for CLIs with no system-prompt flag (Codex, Cursor)
task.body:
The harness owns one canonical set of working rules — the methodology and behavioral guidance currently scattered across a project's CLAUDE.md and its includes (minimalism, no-evasion, the pushback mandate, code-style KPIs, the implementer/reviewer handoff, niche tool references). Instead of every target repo carrying and hand-syncing a CLAUDE.md plus an AGENTS.md plus a Cursor rules file, the harness injects its rule set directly into each agent's headless invocation at dispatch time.

Injection is a per-adapter `build_command/1` concern: use the agent's dedicated system-prompt channel where it has one (Claude Code's `--append-system-prompt-file`), and where it does not, either prepend the rules to the task prompt or render them into a harness-generated ephemeral rule file in the throwaway worktree (Codex and Cursor read a native rule file; Grok has neither, so prompt-prepend). Every delivery is rendered from the one canonical source — what this task rules out is a hand-maintained rule file committed to each target repo, not a generated ephemeral one. The verified per-agent CLI surface is recorded in `docs/agent-cli-reference.md`.

The injected set is a curated, filterable subset, not a token dump: it carries methodology plus the harness's own operational instructions to a dispatched agent (you are being driven by harness; the verification stack is the grader; stage, don't self-grade). It deliberately excludes the verification gates — coverage thresholds, dialyzer-zero, credo-strict — because those are enforced by the verification runner (Task 7), not prose the agent is trusted to honor. A target repo's own CLAUDE.md still auto-loads for Claude; harness injection adds its operational layer and gives the other three agents the same rules without a hand-maintained per-agent file.

task.title: Give Port-spawned agents an immediate-EOF stdin
acceptance_criteria: A Port-spawned agent does not stall waiting on stdin
The prompt and argv are passed without shell-quoting hazards
The executable-not-found error path stays clear
task.body:
Headless agent CLIs spawned over an OTP port inherit an open-but-empty stdin pipe. An agent that peeks stdin to support `cat file | agent -p` then stalls waiting for input that never comes: the Claude Code adapter's integration test shows `claude` printing `no stdin data received in 3s, proceeding without it` and eating a flat 3s per run. Other agents (Cursor, Codex, Grok) likely behave the same.

Give every Port-spawned agent process a stdin that is immediately at EOF, so it proceeds without the stall. The clean, shell-quoting-safe approach is the `sh -c '...' "$@"` argv trick — spawn `/bin/sh` with script `exec <agent> "$@" </dev/null` and pass the real agent argv as positional parameters, so no prompt escaping is needed. Decide whether this belongs in the generic `Harness.AgentAdapter.invoke/2` spawn or per-adapter `build_command/1`; if it moves into the generic spawn, preserve the clean `{:error, {:executable_not_found, _}}` signal that the current direct `System.find_executable/1` provides.
task.implemented: Spawn every agent through /bin/sh with an exec wrapper redirecting stdin from /dev/null, so a Port-spawned headless CLI gets an immediate EOF instead of stalling and exiting doing nothing. Fix lives in the generic AgentAdapter Port spawn (not per-adapter); exec keeps the port os_pid the agent itself so terminate/1 still reaches it; executable+argv ride as sh positional parameters so the prompt needs no shell quoting; System.find_executable/1 still gates the executable-not-found path. FakeAdapter gained stdin_eof and echo-text fixtures; new agent_adapter tests cover stdin-EOF and argv-verbatim. Surfaced by the first dogfood run, which exited :no_changes. Suite green (126 incl. integration); dialyzer/credo/doctor/sobelow clean.

task.title: Commit the agent's work to the run branch before worktree teardown
acceptance_criteria: A :committing state runs between running and verifying; the agent's diff is committed to the harness/<id> branch
On a green run the worktree is torn down but the branch commit survives and carries the agent's files
An agent that produced no diff settles :failed with reason :no_changes (verification skipped)
A commit failure settles :failed with reason {:commit_failed, _}
Full suite green incl. new run/worktree tests; dialyzer/credo/doctor clean
task.body:
The dogfood path destroys the deliverable. A run carves a worktree + harness/<id> branch (Harness.Worktree.create), dispatches an agent that edits files in the worktree, runs verification against the working tree, and on a green verdict calls Worktree.finish(:success) -> git worktree remove --force -- which wipes the agent's uncommitted edits. Nothing in Harness.Run or the driver ever commits, so the harness/<id> branch stays at base ref with zero commits. Harness.Worktree's moduledoc claims the verified commits on the branch are the run's deliverable, but no commit is ever made. Existing run tests never caught this: FakeAdapter's :echo/:sleep commands write no files.

Fix: add a :committing lifecycle state to Harness.Run between running and verifying. When the agent terminates, commit the worktree's full diff to the harness/<id> branch via a new Harness.Worktree.commit/2, then verification grades the committed tree. Commit before verify, always. An agent that produced no diff settles :failed with reason :no_changes (verification skipped). This blocks all dogfooding and is the hand-built bootstrap that lets Task 12 onward be dispatched through harness itself. Discovered during Task 8 follow-up.
task.implemented: Added a :committing lifecycle state to Harness.Run between running and verifying, plus Harness.Worktree.commit/2. When the agent terminates, harness stages and commits the worktree's diff to the harness/<id> branch (explicit harness committer identity, set via git -c so it never fails on missing config) before verification grades it. An agent that produced no diff settles :failed/:no_changes (verification skipped); a commit error settles :failed/{:commit_failed, _}. The branch commit now survives finish/3 teardown — the deliverable is no longer destroyed. New reasons :no_changes and {:commit_failed,_} on Run.Result; :committing added to Run/Status state types. FakeAdapter gained :write/:write_then_hang/:break_git fixtures; new run + worktree tests cover commit, no-changes, commit-failure, and work-survives-teardown. Suite green (124 tests), dialyzer/credo/doctor clean.

task.title: Caller-controlled agent environment in the AgentAdapter contract
acceptance_criteria: A caller can add environment variables for a dispatched agent via `Invocation`, without mutating the orchestrator BEAM's own environment
A caller can remove an inherited environment variable for a dispatched agent — the dogfood `System.delete_env("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")` workaround becomes unnecessary
The adapter conformance suite verifies both env injection and env scrubbing, and every adapter passes it
out_of_scope: Quota/billing detection or fail-over routing — marking a quota-exhausted agent unavailable is Task 16
Secret management or credential vaulting — harness passes through whatever env the caller specifies; it does not store credentials
task.body:
Harness Port-spawns every headless agent inheriting the orchestrator BEAM's environment wholesale — `Harness.AgentAdapter.spawn_run/5` opens the port layering only the adapter's `build_command/1` env additions on top, and `Harness.AgentAdapter.Invocation` carries no environment field at all. The operator has no lever to shape what a dispatched agent sees: they cannot add a per-run variable, and they cannot scrub an inherited one — e.g. remove an inherited `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` so `claude` falls back to its subscription OAuth credentials instead of a (possibly unfunded) API key. That exact gap forced the dogfood driver to call `System.delete_env/1` on the whole BEAM as a workaround.

Give the caller a first-class mechanism, carried on `Invocation`, to both set and unset environment variables for the spawned agent — threaded through every adapter's `build_command/1` and the port spawn (note `port_env/1` currently cannot express a removal: `{key, false}` would crash `String.to_charlist/1`). Cover it in the adapter conformance suite so every adapter honors it identically.

task.title: Antigravity headless adapter
acceptance_criteria: Create Harness.AgentAdapter.Antigravity module implementing Harness.AgentAdapter behaviour
Implement capabilities/0 declaring support for :session_resume, :streaming_output, and :autonomous permission modes
Implement build_command/1 for Antigravity invocation, handling -p, --dangerously-skip-permissions, and --continue flags
Reject unsupported models with {:error, {:unsupported_model, model}}
Unit tests cover all capabilities, build_command/1 scenarios, and message classification
Integrate :antigravity into Harness.Roadmap and Harness.Roadmap.Item valid agents lists
task.body:
Support Antigravity CLI (`agy`) as a headless coding agent adapter in Harness.

The adapter will invoke the `agy` CLI using the `--print` (`-p`) flag for headless execution, `--dangerously-skip-permissions` for autonomous execution, and `--continue` (`-c`) for session resumption. The `agy` CLI does not support a custom model flag, so it will return `{:error, {:unsupported_model, model}}` if a model is specified.

The integration includes registering the `:antigravity` agent in `Harness.Roadmap` and `Harness.Roadmap.Item`, and verifying compliance via an adapter-specific unit test suite.
task.implemented: Created Harness.AgentAdapter.Antigravity module implementing the Harness.AgentAdapter behaviour, mapping autonomous permission mode to --dangerously-skip-permissions, supporting session resumption with --continue, and rejecting model overrides with {:error, {:unsupported_model, model}}. Integrated :antigravity into Harness.Roadmap and Harness.Roadmap.Item. Added unit tests and conformance tests under test/harness/agent_adapter/ verifying capabilities, build_command, and integration.

task.title: Hoist universal adapter callbacks into the AgentAdapter behaviour
acceptance_criteria: A new adapter implementing only build_command/1 + capabilities/0 compiles and passes the conformance suite
All existing adapters keep passing the conformance suite unchanged
Duplicated classify_message/2 and terminate/1 bodies are removed from the adapter modules
task.body: Building the Codex, Cursor, Grok and Antigravity adapters surfaced that classify_message/2, terminate/1, and the --model argv helper are byte-identical across every adapter (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Antigravity, FakeAdapter). Hoist them into the behaviour via `use Harness.AgentAdapter` + defoverridable, so a new adapter declares only what is genuinely agent-specific (build_command/1, capabilities/0). Not an abstraction leak — the contract held — but pure duplication every new adapter re-copies. Surfaced by the first parallel dogfood batch (Tasks 13-15).

task.title: Wire the retry policy into the batch orchestrator
acceptance_criteria: A transient failure in a batch run is retried per the injected RetryPolicy before its result lands in the batch result
A quota-exhausted or terminal failure is not retried — it settles into the batch result immediately
The concurrency cap is respected while retries are in flight
The retry policy is injectable per batch and defaults from :harness, :retry_policy
out_of_scope: Quota fail-over to a different agent — that is the capability registry's job (Task 16)
The repair loop — Task 11's :verification_red feedback is distinct from transient-failure retry
task.body: Harness.Run.RetryPolicy (Task 10) ships as an injectable helper — RetryPolicy.run/2 wraps a `fn -> Result.t()` loop — but nothing calls it. Harness.Batch (Task 9) was built in the same parallel dogfood batch off the same HEAD, so it fans runs out but never applies the retry policy: a transient failure (a process crash, a flaky check) in a batch run is reported, not retried. Wire the retry policy into the batch orchestrator so each run's lifecycle is wrapped by RetryPolicy.run/2, with the policy injectable per batch via the :retry_policy opt already documented on Harness.Run.Supervisor.start_run/4. Transient failures retry with capped backoff; quota-exhausted and terminal failures are not retried — they settle into the batch result as-is. The concurrency cap must still hold while retries are in flight. Surfaced by the parallel multi-agent dogfood batch that delivered Tasks 9-11.

task.title: Force-settle the Run lifetime timeout when the agent handle never arrives
acceptance_criteria: A run whose `{:run_handle}` message never arrives still settles within `lifetime_timeout`
The settled `Result`/`Status` carries a failure reason identifying the never-spawned cause
An agent that spawned just before the lifetime timeout is still cleaned up (SIGKILL or handed to the sweeper)
A regression test drives the never-arrives path and asserts the run force-settles
task.body:
`Harness.Run`'s last-resort lifetime budget (`lifetime_timeout`) currently only force-settles a run once the agent run handle has arrived. If the `{:run_handle}` message never arrives — a hung `build_command`/`invoke` before the agent spawns — the lifetime timeout defers instead of settling, so a wedged run can sit forever and the budget is not actually enforced.

Make the lifetime timeout the genuine last-resort guarantee: when it fires, the run settles (`:failed`, with a reason naming the never-spawned cause) regardless of whether a run handle exists yet. Decide and document the trade-off — force-settling may orphan a just-spawned agent to the `Worktree.Sweeper`, which is acceptable for a last-resort budget.

Surfaced by the post-merge audit of 53cc3ef — see `.audit/53cc3ef-supervised-run-lifecycle.md` finding 3 (a `discuss-design` divergence: Codex rated it pri 8, Claude assessed it latent for the shipped adapters).

task.title: Pin Worktree.commit/2 to the run's harness/<id> branch
acceptance_criteria: `commit/2` lands the commit on the run's `harness/<id>` branch even if the agent moved or detached HEAD, OR fails with a dedicated error rather than committing off-branch
The failure path returns a typed `Harness.Worktree` error and `Harness.Run` settles the run cleanly on it
A test simulates an agent moving HEAD and asserts the deliverable is not stranded
out_of_scope: Restricting which git operations the agent may run inside the worktree
task.body:
`Harness.Worktree.commit/2` captures the agent's work by committing whatever the worktree's HEAD currently points at. The whole deliverable model assumes the work lands on the run's `harness/<id>` branch — but an agent that runs `git switch` or detaches HEAD makes `commit/2` land the commit off-branch, and worktree teardown then loses the run's deliverable.

Make `commit/2` pin its commit to the worktree's own `harness/<id>` branch, or fail loudly if HEAD has moved. The audit noted three options — assert HEAD is on the expected branch and fail with a dedicated error, force-checkout the branch before committing, or commit against an explicit branch ref. Pick one and carry the ripple: a new `Harness.Worktree` error variant and the matching `committing`-state handling in `Harness.Run`.

Surfaced by the post-merge audit of f53b50c — see `.audit/f53b50c-commit-agent-delivery.md` (a `discuss-design` divergence; uncommon trigger but a real deliverable-loss gap).

task.title: Resolve the rmap-delegate ingest gap for the Grok and Antigravity adapters
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded: extend `rmap delegate` to all adapters, or formalize the claude/codex/cursor-rendered-prompt contract for non-delegatable ones
If formalizing: `Harness.Roadmap`, the `@valid_agents` comment, and the agent-facing docs state the contract explicitly
If extending rmap: every harness adapter is a valid `ingest/2` agent, with a regression test per adapter
task.body:
`rmap delegate --to` accepts only `claude` / `codex` / `cursor`, and `Harness.Roadmap` deliberately shells out to `rmap delegate` to render task prompts — so `@valid_agents` on the ingest surface mirrors that set. harness now also ships Grok and Antigravity adapters, which have no ingest path: `ingest(agent: :grok)` / `ingest(agent: :antigravity)` are rejected by design, and those adapters run only with a claude/codex/cursor-rendered prompt dispatched directly via `Harness.Run.start_run/4`. This gap already produced one bug — the `:antigravity` value wrongly admitted to `@valid_agents`, fixed in the 25ed795 audit.

Resolve it deliberately: either extend rmap's `delegate --to` surface to cover every harness adapter, or formally accept that non-delegatable adapters run with a claude/codex/cursor-rendered prompt and document that contract clearly (in `Harness.Roadmap`, the `@valid_agents` rationale comment, and the dogfooding / agent-reference docs).

Surfaced by the post-merge audit of 25ed795 — see `.audit/25ed795-antigravity-headless-adapter.md`.
